questions.enonce_markdown:
Give any TWO differences between export trade and import trade.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Export trade** is the **sale of goods and services to other countries**; **import trade** is the **purchase of goods and services from other countries**.

| Point | Export trade | Import trade |
|---|---|---|
| Direction of goods | Goods **leave** the country and go abroad. | Goods **enter** the country from abroad. |
| Effect on foreign exchange | The country **earns** foreign currency. | The country **spends** foreign currency. |
| Effect on the balance of trade | Exports are a credit item (they increase receipts). | Imports are a debit item (they increase payments). |
| Role of the trader | The local trader is the **seller**, who must find foreign customers and pack and ship the goods. | The local trader is the **buyer**, who must pay the foreign supplier and clear the goods at customs. |

(Any two differences, clearly stated, earn full marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline FOUR reasons for trade protection.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Trade protection** (protectionism) means the use of measures such as import duties (tariffs), quotas, subsidies and import bans to shield local producers from foreign competition. Governments give the following reasons for it.

1. **To protect infant (new) industries.** A young local industry is small and has high costs; it cannot compete with large foreign firms. Protection gives it time to grow and become efficient.

2. **To protect local employment.** Cheap imports may force local firms to close and workers to lose their jobs. Restricting imports keeps local firms and jobs.

3. **To correct a balance of payments deficit.** Limiting imports reduces the amount of foreign currency that leaves the country, so that the gap between imports and exports becomes smaller.

4. **To prevent dumping.** Foreign firms may sell goods abroad at very low prices, below cost, to ruin local producers. Duties on such goods defend the local industry.

(Other correct points: to protect industries that are important for national security or food supply; to raise revenue for the government through customs duties; to avoid depending on other countries for essential goods; to protect the health and safety of consumers; to reduce the use of foreign currency on luxuries.)

**Conclusion.** Trade protection helps local producers and the balance of payments in the short run, but it can raise prices for consumers and provoke retaliation, so it must be used with care.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain any FOUR factors that have encouraged the growth of foreign trade.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Foreign trade** is the buying and selling of goods and services between countries. It has grown strongly for several reasons.

1. **Differences in natural resources and climate.** No country has all the resources it needs; one has oil, another cocoa or timber. Countries trade to obtain what they cannot produce or can produce only at high cost.

2. **Improved transport.** Large ships, containers, aeroplanes, better roads and railways carry goods quickly, safely and cheaply over long distances, which makes it easy to sell abroad.

3. **Improved communication.** The telephone, e-mail, internet and mobile phones allow traders to find customers and suppliers, negotiate and place orders quickly in any part of the world.

4. **Development of banking, insurance and payment facilities.** Banks provide foreign exchange, letters of credit and bank drafts, and insurers cover goods in transit. Buyers and sellers who do not know each other can therefore trade with confidence.

5. **Specialisation and comparative advantage.** Countries produce what they make best and trade for the rest, which lowers costs and raises output.

6. **Trade agreements and trade blocs.** Agreements between countries or regions (for example regional trading groups) reduce customs duties and other barriers, which encourages trade among members.

(Any four factors, each explained, earn full marks. Other points: growth of population and demand, higher incomes, multinational companies, trade fairs and exhibitions, government export promotion.)

**Conclusion.** These factors have made countries more dependent on one another and have raised the volume of foreign trade.
